midwifeInfo.paragraph: Texas licenses Certified Nurse-Midwives (CNMs) through the Texas Board of Nursing, and they practice at Medical City Frisco, Baylor Scott & White Medical Center, and Texas Health Frisco. Texas also licenses Certified Professional Midwives (CPMs) through the Texas Department of State Health Services, making it one of the few states that legally recognizes CPMs for out-of-hospital births. The Frisco Midwifery & Birth Center offers birth center and home birth services with Licensed Midwives (LM) and Certified Professional Midwives (CPM). Families in Frisco have the full spectrum of midwifery care options from hospital-based CNMs to freestanding birth center CPMs.
midwifeInfo.credentialDetail: Texas licenses Certified Nurse-Midwives (CNMs), Certified Professional Midwives (CPMs), and Licensed Midwives (LMs), making it one of the most midwife-friendly states for out-of-hospital birth options.

localDoulas.name: Mya Daniel
localDoulas.credential: Certified Birth & Postpartum Doula, Yoga Teacher
localDoulas.description: Mya Daniel is a certified birth and postpartum doula and yoga teacher with 5 years of experience serving Frisco and the DFW area. She specializes in natural births and believes every woman should have the opportunity to birth on her own terms. Mya provides evidence-based education, emotional support, and hands-on care, empowering families to make informed decisions that align with their values. She is recommended by the Frisco Birth Center and has received praise from midwives for her skill and calming presence.

localDoulas.name: Maggie Wells
localDoulas.credential: Certified Doula, HypnoBirthing Educator, Spinning Babies Educator
localDoulas.description: Maggie Wells has been a full-time certified doula since 2016, serving Denton, Frisco, and the greater DFW area. She is a Trained For Birth Doula, HypnoBirthing Educator, Spinning Babies Educator, and NRP Certified for Birth Assisting. Maggie was named DFW Child Magazine's Child Mom Approved Runner-Up Best Doula of 2022. She provides emotional support, physical comfort, and communication to help families make informed decisions during labor, with expertise in optimal fetal positioning and comfort techniques.

localDoulas.name: Alice Perez
localDoulas.description: Alice Perez is an internationally certified birth doula through BEST Doulas, serving all of Grayson and Collin County including Frisco with deliveries as far as central Dallas. As a mother who has experienced both hospital and home birth, Alice is passionate about educating women and taking away the fear surrounding birth. She helps families feel informed, empowered, and in control of their birth experience. Alice is recommended by the Frisco Birth Center and known for her personalized approach to birth support.

localDoulas.name: Cheryl Johnson
localDoulas.description: Cheryl Johnson is one of the most experienced doulas in the Frisco area, offering hypnoBirthing and holistic birth support through OmBalance. With years of experience serving the DFW metroplex, Cheryl and her team are known as the OGs of the Frisco birth community. She specializes in hypnobirthing techniques and creating beautiful, calm birth experiences. Cheryl is recommended by the Frisco Birth Center as one of their most trusted doula partners.

localDoulas.name: T'Arah Craig
localDoulas.description: T'Arah Craig operates Mother Bear Doula Services in Frisco, serving families across the DFW metroplex with a focus on LGBTQ+ inclusive and culturally responsive birth support. She is recommended by Frisco Midwifery and Birth Center as one of their trusted doula partners, having attended births at Medical City Frisco, Baylor Scott and White, and home births with the birth center. T'Arah brings a particular strength in supporting first-time parents through their labor journey, with training in spinning babies techniques and comfort measures for unmedicated birth. She offers both birth and postpartum packages with flexible payment options.

localDoulas.name: Cheryl Walker
localDoulas.description: Cheryl Walker is a seasoned birth doula and childbirth educator in the Frisco area. She teaches labor coping skills at the Frisco Birth Center and is known as everyone's best friend and aunt in the birth space. Cheryl brings warmth, experience, and deep community connections to every birth she attends, making her one of the most trusted doulas in the Frisco birth community.

hospitalDetails.name: Medical City Frisco
hospitalDetails.paragraph: Medical City Frisco offers a luxurious women's unit with 13 spacious delivery and recovery rooms, 2 dedicated operating rooms for C-sections, and a 6-bed Level III NICU. The hospital supports all birthing options including doula support and VBAC, with pain management options including epidurals, hot and cold therapy, and IV pain control. Amenities include skin-to-skin contact, rooming-in, lactation support, celebratory meals, and 55-inch TVs with streaming services. The hospital offers childbirth preparation courses and free maternity tours. Medical City Frisco provides seamless access to higher-level neonatal care through Medical City Children's Hospital with a Level IV NICU.

hospitalDetails.name: Baylor Scott & White Medical Center - Frisco
hospitalDetails.paragraph: Baylor Scott & White Medical Center in Frisco is a CMS Birthing-Friendly designated hospital and member of the Alliance for Innovation on Maternal Health (AIM). The Women's Center features luxurious suites designed to look like home rather than hospital rooms, with wireless fetal monitoring that allows moms to move freely during labor. The hospital offers 24-hour nursery care, GPS baby security monitoring, specialized lactation support, and skilled labor and delivery nurses. Baylor Frisco has delivered over 30,000 babies since opening and consistently ranks in the 99th percentile for patient experience. The NICU staff is available 24 hours a day for newborns requiring additional care.

hospitalDetails.name: Texas Health Hospital Frisco
hospitalDetails.paragraph: Texas Health Frisco is a CMS Birthing-Friendly designated hospital offering modern, spacious labor and delivery suites with private environments for families. The hospital provides comprehensive pain management options including IV medication, nitrous oxide, epidurals, and aromatherapy patches, along with birthing balls and labor bars for support. Texas Health Frisco offers gentle cesarean births with clear drapes for family-centered delivery, skin-to-skin contact in the golden hour, and spacious two-room postpartum suites. The hospital has a Level II NICU for newborns needing additional care, lactation support, and is an approved breastmilk collection depot for Mother's Milk Bank of North Texas.

birthCenterDetails.name: Frisco Midwifery & Birth Center
birthCenterDetails.paragraph: Frisco Midwifery & Birth Center is a freestanding birth center owned by Margie Wallis, LM, CPM, offering evidence-based holistic midwifery care in the heart of Frisco's Rail District. The center provides both birth center and home birth services, blending modern midwifery tools with holistic care. Services include water birth, pelvic floor physical therapy with Dr. Cara Hartoon, and massage therapy with Mario Vasquez. The center is conveniently located 1 mile from Medical City Frisco for emergency transfer if needed. Free consultations and tours are available, and the center maintains a trusted network of recommended doulas for comprehensive birth support.

costContext.contextParagraph: In Frisco, TX, birth doula packages typically range from $800 to $2,500 with a median price of $1,000. Postpartum doulas average $35 per hour, with rates typically ranging from $30 to $45 per hour. The DFW metroplex has a robust doula community with 180+ providers listed on Bornbir. About 12% of Frisco-area doulas accept insurance including Medicaid. Most doulas offer free consultations, and families are encouraged to interview 2-3 doulas to find the right fit.

culture: Frisco is one of the fastest-growing cities in America, known for its family-friendly communities, excellent schools, and world-class sports facilities including The Star (Dallas Cowboys headquarters). The city's diverse population includes a large South Asian community, and many doulas in the area offer culturally responsive care. Frisco's birth community is anchored by the Frisco Midwifery and Birth Center, which has created a collaborative network of midwives, doulas, and birth professionals serving the DFW metroplex.

faqs.q: How much does a doula cost in Frisco, TX?
faqs.a: Birth doula packages in Frisco typically range from 800 to 2,500 dollars, with a median price of 1,000 dollars. Postpartum doulas average 35 dollars per hour. Most doulas offer free consultations so you can find the right fit for your family.

faqs.q: Does Texas Medicaid cover doula services in Frisco?
faqs.a: Yes, Texas Medicaid covers doula services through the Healthy Texas Women program. Contact your Medicaid managed care plan for specific coverage details and approved providers in the Frisco area.

faqs.q: Are there birth centers in Frisco?
faqs.a: Yes, Frisco Midwifery and Birth Center at 7258 Elm Street offers freestanding birth center and home birth services with Licensed Midwives and Certified Professional Midwives. They offer water birth, prenatal care, and holistic midwifery services.

faqs.q: What hospitals in Frisco have NICUs?
faqs.a: Medical City Frisco has a Level III NICU with 6 beds and 24/7 neonatologist coverage. Baylor Scott and White Frisco and Texas Health Frisco both have Level II NICUs with specialized staff available 24 hours a day.

faqs.q: Can I have a VBAC in Frisco?
faqs.a: Yes, Medical City Frisco explicitly supports VBAC (vaginal birth after cesarean). Baylor Scott and White and Texas Health Frisco also support VBAC with appropriate medical clearance. Discuss your VBAC plans with your OB-GYN and doula.

All three hospitals in Frisco - Medical City Frisco, Baylor Scott and White, and Texas Health Frisco - welcome doulas and labor coaches. Each hospital supports doula involvement during labor and delivery.
